pr_title: lib: os: spsc_pbuf: Add support for full capacity packets
pr_body:
Currently, a largest packet that can be stored in an empty packet buffer was approx. half of the capacity. That is because of a rule that producer modifies only the write index and consumer only the read index. There are cases when user expects that a buffer will be able to hold packets of size much closer to the buffer full capacity.

Adding such feature requires producer to modify the read index (but only when the buffer is empty). With certain limitations that still can perform reliably but because of limitations this mode of operation is optional, enabled by the configuration flag.

To support this option spsc_pbuf_free had to be changed to return an information if freed packet is the last one. Same with spsc_pbuf_read where additional parameter was added (set to null for backward compatibility).

Commit updates test and ipc_service to the modified API.

Fixes #59443.
pr_comments: @emob-nordic @nordic-krch you folks should take ownership of this part in the `CODEOWNERS` file.
If you could leave only the part fixing #59443 i would be grateful.

> Violating the assumption that reader is only modifying read index and writer the write index may end up with hard to spot race conditions.

Now, I'm not very into the technical details of this patch but this statement from @emob-nordic is very true, and especially so when you have caches in the picture.

issue_context.title: os: lib: spsc_pbuf: spsc_pbuf_free does not care if correct len is passed.
comments:
In you proposal what would be the reason for `buf` and `len` in the `spsc_pbuf_free` argument list? If it is to confirm if `len` is correct then it is redundant for me.
 
What about just `spsc_pbuf_free(struct spsc_pbuf *pb, char *buf)` or even `spsc_pbuf_free(struct spsc_pbuf *pb);` for freeing last packet (claimed or not).

> In you proposal what would be the reason for `buf` and `len` in the `spsc_pbuf_free` argument list? If it is to confirm if `len` is correct then it is redundant for me.
> 
> What about just `spsc_pbuf_free(struct spsc_pbuf *pb, char *buf)` or even `spsc_pbuf_free(struct spsc_pbuf *pb);` for freeing last packet (claimed or not).

You are right. I didn't think about it this way. Imo `spsc_pbuf_free(struct spsc_pbuf *pb, char *buf)` is better option.
As a user i expect i should provide the buffer i want to release.

If we go for `spsc_pbuf_free(struct spsc_pbuf *pb)` there is less control over it. User may accidentally free twice which will result in data drop. Still, that's just my opinion.

review_comments: sorry to picky about this but is this barrier supposed to wait for the cache op to be completed? Because in that case you need `barrier_dsync_fence_full()` instead.
